artifacts.summary:
The one authorized sentence was corrected and nothing else moved. Doc lines 46-47 now read that the probe fires on session_ended, that most harnesses do not emit that event today, and that most rows therefore carry null. Both constraints held: zero harness names and zero counts, so the wording cannot go stale inside a section promoted verbatim, and the word six now appears nowhere in the file.

The reviewer proved the replacement from the adapters rather than from the gate's account of them. Claude and Gemini both register SessionEnd and map it. Codex has an adapter and still cannot emit: its event table carries no SessionEnd key and its hook manifest registers eight events, none of them that one. Antigravity emits a single event and it is store_changed. Six harnesses have no adapter at all. So eight of ten rows can never be probed and most is true. The replacement also repairs a defect beyond the one the gate named: no event adapter was the wrong predicate, because two of the four adapter-bearing harnesses still cannot emit the event, so the original over-promised coverage by two rows.

Scope was confirmed by diff rather than by re-reading. The range between the two heads is one file, one hunk, three added and four removed, entirely inside the authorized paragraph, so the fsmonitor wording's absent run count, the race characterisation and the working-directory claim could not have moved. Spot checks agree, and twice, unconditional and finished_at all remain at zero occurrences.

All three checks were confirmed by API to belong to the current head rather than a superseded one, and the five skips were proven to be the filtered kind from the aggregator's own gating condition rather than from their label. Copilot left no review comments and no reviews. One observation was recorded and deliberately not routed: the PR body still says 103 lines where the head is 102, which the implementation named in a PR comment, and correcting it would mean editing the body the gate's do-not-change list protects.

The FO arbiter reproduced the corrected text independently at the pushed SHA and from the GitHub contents API. Both are byte-identical at checksum fb55ad03, so the content that will merge is the content that was reviewed.
